reader.requirement: At --std 85 an entry that writes both EXTERNAL and REDEFINES must be refused, while a separate entry that REDEFINES an external record (X.4.5.4 GR2) stays legal.
reader.edition-search: ClausePlacementRules.Rules and DataBinder#ScreenClausePlacement / ClausePlacementRule#ResidenceFault consult no edition (grep CobolVersion|IsAtLeast|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior over DataBinder.ClausePlacement.cs: only Edition.Error). The one row term a later edition adds, TypeDeclarationInAnySection (EXTERNAL on a level 1 TYPEDEF anywhere), is unreachable at 85 because VersionConformancePass refuses TYPEDEF below 2002 (probe x2td.cob).

reader.notes: The NotWith row (EXTERNAL excluded with REDEFINES|BASED) refuses the combination and drops the EXTERNAL, so the redefines anchor is not re-based onto the external cell. Edition-independent; BASED cannot be written at 85.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: x1ord.cob '01 ALT-R IS EXTERNAL REDEFINES BASE-R' (EXTERNAL written before REDEFINES) refused COBOL2404 (SR3) and COBOL2739 (REDEFINES position), while '01 GLB-R REDEFINES BASE-R IS GLOBAL' in the same program drew nothing; x1lvl.cob a REDEFINES on a SUBORDINATE entry of an EXTERNAL record (not the same entry) compiled and ran correctly; x1as.cob 'IS EXTERNAL BASED' refused COBOL0900 (BASED is 2002) plus COBOL2404. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.4.3.3 SR3  (4.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'.
